title: Normalized purity transposes with their scalar square and shifts
statement: Under the geometric and coefficient hypotheses of [def-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality-data], there exist a normalized exceptional coefficient System S and ComparisonData P for it such that its gamma, a and b satisfy the purity scalar square and gamma is compatible with the recorded source and exceptional shifts. This constructs natural invertible transposes with their exact finite reductions and coefficient-mate normalization; it does not assert the source or exceptional unit, associativity, or scalar-comparison shift equations.

source.place: Integral coefficient transport and compatibility; extracted assembly below lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality

proof.text: Construct the coefficient System and restrict the actual operations to the uniform finite-Tor domains. Transport source and compact-support scalar comparisons by their ordinary/completed realization comparisons, retaining component normalizations. The finite right realization is pinned by the fixed-scalar Hom-transpose equation independently of gamma.

Reconstruct a base-field unit orientation, form its trace, and extend that same trace to each finite coefficient field. The unit-trace construction gives natural invertible transposes, coefficient linearity and every prescribed finite reduction. Its normalized realization produces targetRealizationReductions and finiteReductions, without asserting uniqueness of arbitrary lifts.

Scalar coherence for extensions of this one trace and the conditional coefficient calculus give the purity scalar square after transport through the canonical source and scalar coordinates. The recorded counit transpose gives bMate.

Apply projection shift coherence to the same shifted unit and trace. Transport its two shift identities through the canonical source reassociation, whose crossing sign is (-1)^(2d)=1. The shift calculus gives gamma compatibility with the recorded source and exceptional shifts.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedComparisonConstruction :
    ∃ (S : ConstructibleExceptionalCoefficients.System C.l C.Qbar D C.different (f := f))
      (P : ComparisonData D C f d S),
    (∀ (E F : Field D C) (h : E ≤ F) (K : Cat D C E Y),
    (scalar D C P.scalarClosed E F h true).map ((P.gamma E).hom.app K) ≫
        (P.b E F h).hom.app K =
      (P.a E F h).hom.app K ≫
        (P.gamma F).hom.app ((scalar D C P.scalarClosed E F h false).obj K)) ∧
    (∀ (E : Field D C),
    ShiftCompatibility (source D C f d E) (target D C f S E)
      (sourceShift D C f d E) (targetShift D C f S E) (P.gamma E))
